mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over three consecutive quarters signals weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for three quarters but S&P 500 forward returns remain positive in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 2% annualized growth over two consecutive quarters signals robust manufacturing expansion, which historically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to improved corporate earnings prospects.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises above 2% annualized for two quarters but S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% triggers a tightening cycle that increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as equity valuations compress.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 forward returns remain positive in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% over three consecutive months signals labor market tightness, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three months but S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.
